newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen in range, await Greenspan, auction.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen in range, await Greenspan, auction.

text.p: Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are expected to spend Tuesday trapped in a narrow range amid a dearth of fresh factors, with operators sidelining themselves ahead of Congressional testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan later on Tuesday and a bond auction on Wednesday, traders said.

Greenspan is scheduled to deliver his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to a House of Representatives subcommittee at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT on Tuesday. While this will have no direct impact on the JGB market, traders are watching for spillover effects from U.S. market moves.
"If Greenspan says something that sends the Dow sharply lower, we'd see a response in the Nikkei, and this would affect JGBs," one trader wth a trust bank's securities arm said.

Operators are also waiting for the results of a Wednesday auction of 10-year bonds. Traders said the prospective coupon, at 2.4 to 2.5 percent, is likely to be attractive to buyers and could boost the key bond if the results are favourable.

But with few other factors, Tuesday trade is expected to be lacklustre, with resistance expected to develop near last week's high of 125.30, while a continuing shift to guardedly positive sentiment will keep the downside underpinned.
